mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3pp in three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% in three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 2% over three months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 2% in three months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high federal funds rate (above 4.5%) is associated with lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased borrowing costs and reduced investment.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% each over three months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where both PAYEMS increased and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5% in three months.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% during a period of economic expansion signals a potential slowdown in consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 1% during an economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and decrease in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% each over three months signals an increase in supply efficiency, which can lead to deflationary pressures and reduced corporate pricing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where both INDPRO increased and CPIAUCSL decreased by more than 0.5% in three months.
